stubs.angle: When does a two-way WPF binding on TextBox.Text write the typed value back to the view model property by default?
stubs.answerHinge: The default UpdateSourceTrigger for TextBox.Text is LostFocus, so the source is updated when the text box loses focus, not on every keystroke, unless PropertyChanged is set explicitly.

stubs.angle: Why does a view model bound to WPF or MAUI controls implement INotifyPropertyChanged, and what happens on screen if it does not?
stubs.answerHinge: The binding engine subscribes to PropertyChanged and re-reads only the named property when the event fires; without the event a changed plain CLR property is never pushed to the bound control.

stubs.angle: In .NET 8 and later Blazor, where does component code execute when a component uses the InteractiveServer render mode?
stubs.answerHinge: With InteractiveServer the component runs on the server; browser events travel to it over a SignalR circuit and the server sends back UI diffs, whereas InteractiveWebAssembly runs the code in the browser.

stubs.angle: With @bind on an input element and no extra modifiers, when is the bound C# field updated as the user types?
stubs.answerHinge: @bind on an input uses the onchange event by default, so the field updates when the element loses focus after a change; @bind:event="oninput" is needed to update on every keystroke.

stubs.angle: A list control is bound to an ObservableCollection<T> of plain item classes; which of the listed changes does the list show without any extra code?
stubs.answerHinge: ObservableCollection<T> raises CollectionChanged for Add, Remove, Insert and Clear, but not when a property of an existing item changes (that needs INotifyPropertyChanged on the item) or when the view model property is reassigned to a new collection without its own notification.

stubs.angle: A runnable BCL view model with a subscriber that prints received property names raises PropertyChanged with a copy-pasted string name in one setter, so the change of that property is never reported; find the line.
stubs.answerHinge: The binding engine matches the event by property name, so a setter that raises PropertyChanged with another property's name leaves its own bindings stale; nameof or [CallerMemberName] prevents the mismatch.

stubs.angle: A Blazor component updates a counter in a System.Threading.Timer callback and calls StateHasChanged directly; find the line that fails at run time.
stubs.answerHinge: A timer callback runs outside the renderer's dispatcher, so StateHasChanged throws that the current thread is not associated with the Dispatcher; the call must be wrapped in InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged).

stubs.angle: Which of the listed events make a ComponentBase-derived Blazor component re-render without an explicit StateHasChanged call?
stubs.answerHinge: ComponentBase re-renders automatically after its own event handlers complete, after receiving new parameters from a re-rendering parent and after lifecycle methods finish; a field changed by a timer or by an injected service raising its own event does not re-render the component on its own.

stubs.angle: A button bound to a custom ICommand stays disabled after the condition checked by CanExecute becomes true; what is missing?
stubs.answerHinge: The bound control queries CanExecute only when the command raises CanExecuteChanged, so the command must raise that event when its condition changes.

stubs.angle: How does BindingContext flow through a .NET MAUI page, and what goes wrong when a child element or a DataTemplate item has a different context than the developer expects?
stubs.answerHinge: BindingContext is inherited down the visual tree unless a child sets its own, and inside a DataTemplate the context is the collection item, so a binding to a page-level command needs an explicit Source (for example a relative source or x:Reference) instead of the inherited context.

stubs.angle: A Blazor app shows a cart counter in the layout header that must update when a product page several levels away adds an item; how do you design the state sharing?
stubs.answerHinge: Use a scoped state container service that holds the cart and raises a change event; subscribing components call InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged) in the handler and unsubscribe in Dispose, because a mutable service does not trigger re-rendering by itself and cascading parameters suit values flowing down one subtree rather than sibling updates.

stubs.angle: Why can removing or reordering items in a Blazor list without @key show stale input values or reset the wrong child component, and how does @key fix it?
stubs.answerHinge: Without @key the render-tree diff matches elements and components by position in the sequence, so state is reused for a different item; @key makes the diff match by the key value, preserving or recreating the right element at some extra diff cost.

stubs.angle: A WPF ListBox bound to 100,000 items takes seconds to open and uses a lot of memory after it was moved into a StackPanel inside a ScrollViewer; how do you diagnose and fix it?
stubs.answerHinge: UI virtualization in VirtualizingStackPanel works only when the panel gets a constrained viewport and item scrolling; placing the list in an unbounded StackPanel or ScrollViewer, setting CanContentScroll to false or grouping without virtualization support makes WPF create a container for every item, so the fix is to restore a constrained layout and keep virtualization and container recycling enabled.

stubs.angle: Describe how WPF renders a window: what the retained visual tree is, what the UI thread and the render thread each do, and why a long synchronous handler freezes input while the window can still be redrawn.
stubs.answerHinge: WPF is retained mode: the UI thread owns DispatcherObjects, processes input and layout and updates the visual tree, while a separate render thread composes that tree to the screen, so blocking the UI thread stops input and layout updates but not composition of what is already in the tree.
